propositions: The test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to a per-test timeout of 300s triggered by pytest-timeout's thread method calling os._exit(1).
The test iterates over 884 renderable units in a single function, spawning ~1768 pandoc processes sequentially, measuring 91.6s idle but 504.8s under CPU contention (1.7x the timeout budget).
The test's cost is unbounded and load-dependent, causing intermittent worker crashes on the macOS cell where contention is routine, while identical commits pass on ubuntu cells.
The fix chunks the equivalence test into parametrized cases with a fixed _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK constant, distributing work across xdist workers and bounding per-test cost to ~4.2s each.
A new coverage guard test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit verifies all 884 units are covered and no chunks are silently dropped, preserving the byte-identity property.
The byte-identity property and oracle comparison (_EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE = 1, real pandoc on both sides) remain unchanged; the fix addresses test cost structure, not renderer behavior.
